subject: APAC pinning, temporary cross-region egress, and subprocessor visibility
messages:

Subject: Can Redwood guarantee APAC pinning and clarify temporary cross-region processing?
Attachments: (none)

Hi Dylan,

Quick intro — I'm Priya on the security team at Acme Fintech. We're evaluating Redwood for a production deployment in Singapore and want to confirm a few residency/transfer items before we proceed to procurement:

- Can Redwood guarantee that both inference and analytics (logs/usage) for our tenant can be pinned to APAC (Singapore) region?
- If you have temporary cross-region processing (eg for failover or analytics backfill), what is the maximum window and how is customer data protected during that window?
- Who are the subprocessors specifically operating in APAC, and do any of them have access to unredacted request/response payloads?
- We need to confirm KMS usage for customer-managed keys or ability to escrow keys for region-locked data.

Please share the relevant DPA excerpt or a short note we can include in our risk register. If you have SOC2 or audit evidence to share, that would help speed things up.

Thanks —
Priya Sharma
Security, Acme Fintech
priya@acmefin.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Can Redwood guarantee APAC pinning and clarify temporary cross-region processing?
Attachments: redwood_DPA_v3.pdf; subprocessors_list_2026-07.csv

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear list of asks. High level answers below, followed by attachments and next steps.

1) APAC pinning: Yes — Redwood supports region pinning at the tenant level. For Hosted customers we can configure both inference routing and telemetry pipelines to remain within the APAC region (SG). That is our standard offering for enterprise tiers.

2) Temporary cross-region processing (failover/backfill): We do allow transient cross-region processing only under two conditions: (a) automatic failover when the primary region is unavailable, or (b) customer-authorized backfill for analytics. The standard temporary window is configurable, but we commonly commit to a maximum of 72 hours for automatic failover and up to 7 days for customer-authorized backfill with explicit approval. During any transient window we restrict access via ephemeral tokens and audit the session.

3) Subprocessors: See attached CSV — it lists subprocessors and region of operation. For APAC there are a small set of cloud partners and managed infra providers; none of these subprocessors have access to unredacted production payloads unless a customer elects to share logs for troubleshooting. We redact sensitive request tokens by default; full payload access requires an explicit support ticket and a customer-signed change request.

4) KMS / customer-managed keys: We support BYOK via KMS for encryption at rest. For Private deployments we can use customer-provided keys; for Hosted we offer a customer-managed KMS integration (bring your key via supported cloud KMS providers). We can discuss escrow options if needed — this is an uncommon but supported path under enterprise contracts.

Attached: redwood_DPA_v3.pdf (current DPA draft), subprocessors_list_2026-07.csv (redacted contact info). I'll also drop an engineering tech note that explains transient egress behavior for caches and analytics.

Next steps: Marissa (cc'd) is our account lead; she can coordinate a short legal call if you want redlines on the DPA. Kimberly from infra will follow up with a short technical note on KV cache and replication specifics.

Best,

Subject: APAC pinning — technical detail on transient egress and cache behavior
Attachments: apac_pin_technote.pdf

Hi Priya — Kimberly on the infra team. Quick technical clarification to supplement Dylan's note:

- Serving/runtime: Tenant traffic is routed to SG-based endpoints. Inference compute and primary KV caches remain in-region.
- Transient KV/edge caching: To reduce cold-start latency we keep short-lived edge caches. These caches do not persist long-term and are encrypted in transit and at rest. In a failover event we promote a secondary region (e.g., ap-southeast-1 -> ap-northeast-1) — promotion incurs ephemeral replication of the minimal working set (KV pointers, not raw payloads) and is limited to a 72-hour auto-failover window.
- Analytics/usage pipelines: We can configure analytics aggregation to stay in-region. If you opt into a global analytics stream (for cross-region reporting) we will require your explicit approval.
- Access controls: Subprocessors that operate platform monitoring or autoscaling in APAC will only see metadata and aggregated metrics unless a ticket is raised. We can provide a signed addendum that prohibits full payload access for APAC subprocessors.

I've attached a short tech note that diagrams the failover flow and data categories that may transiently move. Happy to walk through it on a quick call.

Kimberly Park

- DPA language: we need explicit contract wording limiting automatic failover to "temporary, unavoidable disruptions" and capping automatic cross-border processing at 72 hours unless Customer consents. Can you provide suggested language we can include as an addendum?
- DocuSign: once we have the redlines we'd like to circulate the DPA to our procurement team. Is the Docusign link you referenced the canonical DPA?

If you can send the SOC2 and a suggested addendum language, we'll aim to turn around redlines within 3 business days.

Hi Priya — thanks for the questions. Two quick items we can action immediately:

1) SOC2: We can provide our latest SOC2 Type II report (covers hosted production environments) under an NDA. I'll share the secure link after we get an email address for delivery (I can send to security@acmefin.com).

2) Suggested DPA addendum language (draft excerpt) — feel free to copy/paste into your redlines: 

"Temporary Cross-Border Processing: Customer data shall be processed in the APAC region for both inference and telemetry. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may, in the event of unavoidable regional service disruption or with Customer's explicit prior authorization, process Customer data in an alternative region for up to seventy-two (72) consecutive hours for the purpose of failover and continuity. Any processing beyond seventy-two (72) hours requires prior written Customer consent. Redwood shall log and report any such transient processing event to Customer within 24 hours and shall not permit Subprocessors in the alternative region access to unredacted Customer payloads without Customer authorization."

3) DocuSign/DPA: The DocuSign link we shared is the canonical DPA workflow; I've attached a redline (redwood_DPA_v3_redline.pdf) with the above excerpt added and a subsection that prohibits APAC subprocessors from accessing unredacted payloads without ticketed authorization. If that looks good, we can send the DocuSign envelope to your procurement contact and loop in legal for signatures.

Next step: Priya, if you can confirm the delivery address for the SOC2 and who on procurement should receive the DocuSign, we'll push this through. Also happy to schedule a 30-minute legal + infra call to sign off.

Thanks —
